analyst_view.overall: The 111th Nordderby: Daniel Thioune's Werder (6th, 15 points, beaten only once at home this season) host Merlin Polzin's Hamburg (11th, 12 points, only three points from five away games), and Werder have won eight of their last nine home meetings with Hamburg. The big change since this morning: Werder confirmed on Saturday that top creator Marco Gruell (calf) and Mitchell Weiser (thigh) both miss the derby after sitting out the final training session; the numbers already count Weiser but not Gruell, and Justin Njinmah is expected on the wing instead, while Senne Lynen is back from illness and Fuellkrug, the league's top scorer with nine goals (six from set pieces), starts. Hamburg are without Remberg, Nadir, Torunarigha, Sambi Lokonga and Poulsen (the numbers count Poulsen and Sambi Lokonga for goals), but Daka and Muheim were expected back after skipping international duty and Capaldo is reported fit. Florian Badstuebner referees: his low card record (-23%) and the derby boost (+39%) are both in the numbers, and the atmosphere will be hot, with ex-Hamburg captain Ludovit Reis expecting a hostile reception.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already taking about 12% off Hamburg for Poulsen and 3% for Sambi Lokonga, and 4% off Werder for Weiser. Gruell, Werder's main creator (two goals and six assists in nine games per the Bundesliga's site), is now confirmed out and the numbers do not know it, so I move from -4 to -6, about 2.5 goals; Fuellkrug's set pieces keep Werder dangerous even without him.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, most of them for Werder at home against Hamburg's back three with wing-backs. Losing Gruell and Weiser costs Werder some wide play, but Njinmah's pace down the flank and Werder's set-piece focus around Fuellkrug should still win corners, and I found nothing that clearly points either way, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards: they add 39% for the derby but take 23% off for referee Badstuebner, who shows only 3.1 cards a game, and both sides have been booked less than usual lately (all counted). The build-up is heated (fans' bus welcome, Reis facing whistles from the away end), but that is the normal derby feel the numbers already add, so I stay at 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots, lifted by Werder's strong recent volume (+20%), much of it built through Gruell. With Gruell now confirmed out and Weiser (counted for goals only) missing on the right, Werder lose two of their main suppliers, so I go from -2 to -4, about 30.0 shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with Werder's 43 on target in six games already added (+15%). Without Gruell, who set up many of those chances, Werder's openings should be fewer and less clean; now that his absence is confirmed I go from -3 to -5, about 10.3 shots on target.
